$chapter.source: wp-content/mu-plugins/ (real disk scan 2026-08-31, re-scanned after apollo-webp-force)
$chapter.note: Carved out of 14-routing, which documented only 5 of 15 files. The MU layer is the boot layer — it runs before active_plugins and cannot be switched off from wp-admin, so an undocumented file here is an invisible global side effect. 14-routing keeps $routing_canonical + $third_party_plugins only.

$mu_plugins.description: Must-Use plugins in wp-content/mu-plugins/. Loaded before regular plugins, in ALPHABETICAL filename order, and cannot be deactivated from wp-admin. This is the Apollo boot layer.
$mu_plugins.$load_order_note: WordPress loads mu-plugins alphabetically; there is no dependency resolution. apollo-brain.php sorts first among the apollo-* files, which is why it can hook muplugins_loaded at -100 and still define APOLLO_REGISTRY_PATH before anything reads it. Renaming a file here silently changes boot order.
$boot_sequence: 1. WP loads every mu-plugin file alphabetically (apollo-brain → apollo-debug → apollo-dev-routing → apollo-error-handler → apollo-events-helpers-guard → apollo-force-open-registration → apollo-htaccess-lock → apollo-locale-pt-br → apollo-route-setup → apollo-webp-force → elementor-safe-mode → endurance-page-cache → force-load-apollo-events → force-load-apollo-login → force-load-apollo-telegram → force-load-apollo-templates)
2. apollo-brain hooks muplugins_loaded @ -100 → defines APOLLO_REGISTRY_PATH, require_once apollo-core.php
3. apollo-core registers its own bootstrap on plugins_loaded @ 1 (CPT/Meta/security init happens THERE, not in the brain)
4. force-load-* files require their plugin main file directly, bypassing active_plugins
5. apollo-route-setup runs its one-time maintenance on init @ 20
6. apollo-webp-force registers three image filters; nothing runs until an image is actually processed

apollo-brain.description: THE BRAIN. Earliest Apollo code to run. Defines APOLLO_REGISTRY_PATH, validates the runtime registry JSON parses, require_once apollo-core/apollo-core.php so Core registers its bootstrap before active_plugins is processed, installs the script defer filter, and wires registry/page cache purge.
does: json_decode validation of that file — logs to error_log only when WP_DEBUG_LOG, never die()s in production
script_loader_tag filter: adds defer to front-end scripts, with an explicit allow-list that must stay synchronous
transition_post_status @ 999 → apollo_purge_all() + Registry::clear_cache() on first publish only
does_not: Does NOT init CPT / Meta / FieldEncryption / HMAC / SEOTextBlock / PaneMode — apollo_core_bootstrap() on plugins_loaded P1 owns all of that, so ordering is guaranteed and nothing double-inits
Does NOT load the registry JSON into a constant — Apollo\Core\Registry + object cache own that, to avoid duplicating ~2.3 MB in RAM
defer_hard_exclusions: cdn.apollo.rio.br/v1(.x)/core.js — matched by regex on src
tags already carrying defer or async

apollo-debug.guard: WP_DEBUG || APOLLO_DEV_MODE — returns immediately otherwise, so production overhead is zero
apollo-debug.description: Query Monitor panel for the Apollo ecosystem plus the apollo_debug_log() helper. Loads after apollo-brain (alphabetical: brain < debug).
panel_shows: Registry path, load status, plugin count
Active Apollo plugins with version + status from the registry
Whether the registry came from object cache or disk
apollo-debug.$notable: Hooks plugins_loaded @ 0 to reset display_errors=0, because the third-party wp-debugging plugin calls @ini_set('display_errors',1) at load time and apollo-core's plugins_loaded @ 1 textdomain notice would otherwise corrupt REST JSON responses.

apollo-dev-routing.guard: APOLLO_DEV_MODE — early return at file level
apollo-dev-routing.description: On template_redirect, records which route handler won into $GLOBALS['apollo_dev_route_handler'] and logs it. Reads apollo_login_page / apollo_home_page / apollo_feed_page query vars and $GLOBALS['apollo_current_route'].

apollo-error-handler.description: Funnels 4xx/5xx through the central Apollo error pages so every plugin and WP core surface the same UX. Hooked last so each plugin still gets first chance to claim its route (e.g. apollo-login's virtual /acesso). Mirrors the Apache ErrorDocument directives in the project .htaccess.
apollo-error-handler.$drift_fixed_2026_08_31: 14-routing described this as 'priority 999' from the docblock prose; the actual add_action calls use PHP_INT_MAX.

apollo-events-helpers-guard.description: Brutal early guarantee that apollo_event_* global helpers exist before any template runs. Force-requires apollo-events main file if not already loaded, calls apollo_event_ensure_helpers(), and defines a fallback apollo_event_parse_date() (with hardcoded pt-BR month/weekday tables) if the real one is missing.
apollo-events-helpers-guard.$risk: Declares global functions with a pt-BR date table duplicated from apollo-events. If apollo-events changes its own parse_date contract, this shim silently keeps serving the old shape whenever the plugin fails to load. Shim, not a feature — retire once apollo-events is reliably active.

apollo-force-open-registration.description: Forces WordPress 'Anyone can register' to READ as enabled. Runs after Really Simple SSL (which filters the same option at 999).
apollo-force-open-registration.$risk: SECURITY-RELEVANT AND INVISIBLE. Overrides the effective value of users_can_register for every read, including REST and wp-admin. The DB option is untouched, so wp-admin shows 'checked' while the stored value may be '0' — anyone auditing the setting in the UI cannot tell it is being forced. Any decision to close registration MUST delete this file; unchecking the box in wp-admin will not work.

apollo-htaccess-lock.description: Restores and read-locks the root .htaccess before regular plugins (NFD / WP core) can truncate it. Thin loader: requires apollo-core/includes/htaccess-lock.php, which holds the real logic.
apollo-htaccess-lock.$note: File header says 'Auto-installed from apollo-core. Do not edit; change the source under plugins/apollo-core/mu-plugins/apollo-htaccess-lock.php' — but the path it actually requires is includes/htaccess-lock.php. Verify which of the two is the live source before editing either.

apollo-locale-pt-br.description: Forces Brazilian Portuguese for all rendered WordPress and Apollo UI strings, front and admin. 8 filters + 2 actions covering gettext, date_i18n and wp_date.
apollo-locale-pt-br.$note: APOLLO_LOCALE = 'pt_BR' (WP slug) and APOLLO_LOCALE_HTML = 'pt-BR' (BCP 47 for HTML lang / JS Intl) are deliberately different strings. Do not collapse them.

apollo-route-setup.description: One-time maintenance, gated on an option flag. Drafts WP Pages whose slugs collide with Apollo virtual routes, clears the Apollo Home template from conflicting pages, re-adds rewrite rules, flushes them, and clears Registry + FrontRouteDispatcher caches.
apollo-route-setup.$drift_fixed_2026_08_31: 14-routing recorded current_flag_example '2026.05.20.2'; disk is '2026.07.03.2'. Bump this flag whenever the reserved slug list changes, or the maintenance never re-runs.
apollo-route-setup.production_guard: On apollo.rio.br / www.apollo.rio.br the page-drafting step is OPT-IN via define('APOLLO_ROUTE_SETUP', true) — so a deploy can never silently unpublish a marketing page that reuses a reserved slug. Rewrite flush + cache clear still run.
apollo-route-setup.reserved_slugs_source: apollo_get_reserved_virtual_slugs() when available; otherwise the hardcoded 22-slug fallback in this file

apollo-webp-force.description: Forces every image size WordPress generates to be written as WebP at quality 80, and prefers Imagick over GD. PHASE 1 ONLY: the uploaded original is deliberately untouched.
filters_hooked: jpeg_quality @ 10 => 82, for any JPEG still generated
actions_hooked: admin_notices — warns only when no editor can write WebP
does_not: Does NOT replace or delete the uploaded original. APOLLO_WEBP_REPLACE_ORIGINAL is defined but deliberately UNREAD until Phase 2.
Does NOT convert gif / webp / avif / svg / ico / bmp / tiff / pdf — by omission: only three keys are ever added to the format map.
Does NOT convert the site icon. WP favicon paths expect PNG, and a broken fallback there shows on every browser tab.
Does NOT register a CPT, meta key, option, REST route or admin page.
apollo-webp-force.$host_capability_2026_08_31: Verified from the live library rather than a probe: attachment 117 (club63-3.webp) carries a full generated WebP subsize set and attachment 187 (festa-selvagem.avif) carries a full AVIF set. WordPress can only produce those through WP_Image_Editor, so Imagick with WebP AND AVIF is live on apollo.rio.br.
apollo-webp-force.$why_mu: The filters do not need the MU layer to work — the format decision happens inside wp_generate_attachment_metadata(), far after plugins_loaded. MU is chosen so a half-converted library cannot be caused by someone deactivating a plugin in wp-admin.
apollo-webp-force.$risk: LOW while Phase 1 stands: three filters, no writes, no state. WordPress core adds its own guard — WP_Image_Editor::get_output_format() honours the mapping only when supports_mime_type() agrees — so an editor without WebP keeps JPEG instead of emitting a broken file. Re-grade this entry to MEDIUM when Phase 2 lands, because Phase 2 deletes originals.
apollo-webp-force.$phase: 1 of 6. Phase 2 (replace original), 3 (existing library via Tools -> Apollo Health), 4 (scope classified-* sizes), 5 (hardening) are not implemented yet.

force-load-apollo-events.description: Requires plugins/apollo-events/apollo-events.php directly so the /evento/ CPT rewrite and apollo_event_* helpers exist regardless of active_plugins. Idempotent via defined('APOLLO_EVENT_FILE'); still re-runs apollo_event_ensure_helpers() on the already-loaded path to survive OPcache drift.

force-load-apollo-login.description: Requires plugins/apollo-login/apollo-login.php so the virtual /acesso route works without wp-admin activation drift. Idempotent via defined('APOLLO_LOGIN_FILE').
force-load-apollo-login.$self_declared_temporary: File header: 'Safe on local; remove when plugin is reliably active in production active_plugins.'

force-load-apollo-templates.description: Requires plugins/apollo-templates/apollo-templates.php so virtual /feed, /casa etc. resolve. Idempotent via defined('APOLLO_TEMPLATES_FILE').

force-load-apollo-telegram.description: Requires plugins/apollo-telegram/apollo-telegram.php so /telegram, ?telegram-test=1 and its REST endpoints are live without activating the plugin.
force-load-apollo-telegram.$risk: The ONLY force-load file with no defined()/idempotency guard and no declare(strict_types=1) — it is a bare file_exists + require_once. Its own header says 'Safe for test only. Remove this file when you activate the plugin normally.' It is still present on a production host.

$force_load_pattern.what: Four mu-plugin files each require a plugin's main file directly, bypassing the WordPress active_plugins option.
$force_load_pattern.why: Guarantees virtual routes and global helpers exist even when a plugin is not activated in wp-admin, or when activation state drifts between environments.
cost: wp-admin's Plugins screen no longer tells the truth: a force-loaded plugin runs whether it shows as active or not, and DEACTIVATING IT THERE DOES NOTHING.
register_activation_hook never fires on this path — a plugin that installs DB tables or seeds options on activation will run without them.
Load order moves from the plugins layer to the MU layer, which is earlier than some plugins expect.
$force_load_pattern.retire_when: The plugin is reliably present in production active_plugins. Three of the four files say so in their own headers.
$force_load_pattern.$risk: MEDIUM — invisible activation state. Anyone debugging 'why is this plugin running / not deactivating' will not find the answer in wp-admin.

elementor-safe-mode.description: Elementor's Safe Mode loader — when enabled, loads only the editor without the theme or any other plugin. Auto-installed by Elementor.
elementor-safe-mode.$risk: If the elementor_safe_mode option is ever switched on, THE ENTIRE APOLLO ECOSYSTEM STOPS LOADING for that session, including every mu-plugin force-load above. Gated on an option + cookie token, so it is inert until triggered.

endurance-page-cache.description: Host-level page cache purging (Bluehost / Endurance stack). Largest file in the MU layer by an order of magnitude.
endurance-page-cache.$relationship_to_brain: apollo-brain's maybe_init_cache_integration() fires apollo/brain/page_cache_maybe_init instead of touching this directly, because Apollo\Core\Cache does not exist in this codebase yet. Purges are coordinated through apollo_purge_single() / apollo_purge_all().

$debris.description: Non-PHP files sitting in the MU directory. Harmless to WordPress (it only scans *.php at the top level) but they are noise, and one is a leaked debug artifact.

debug-1098c0.log.content: NDJSON from debug session 1098c0 — auth-head.php asset URL probes, local dev (aprio.local) paths, timestamps ~2026-06.
debug-1098c0.log.action: DELETE — same family of leftover debug beacon already stripped from apollo-events and apollo-chat.

sync.ffs_db.action: Keep if RealTimeSync mirrors this directory; it is tooling state, not code. Should be gitignored.

$registry_path_warning.severity: HIGH — naming collision that has confused every reader of this registry
$registry_path_warning.problem: TWO different files are called apollo-registry.json.

runtime.purpose: What the SITE reads at request time.

documentation.purpose: The chaptered SSOT's build output. Documentation. NOT read at request time.

$registry_path_warning.relationship: The doc monolith is intended to be deployed to the runtime path — 00-registry-map.json build_rules.output.runtime names it, and build.js explicitly does NOT write it ('runtime target (deploy step, not written here)'). So the deploy step is manual and undocumented, and the two files can silently diverge.
$registry_path_warning.consequence: A chapter edit changes nothing at runtime until someone runs build.js --write AND copies the monolith to wp-content/. Neither step is automated or verified.
$registry_path_warning.$open_question: Nothing in this registry records WHEN the runtime file was last synced, or whether it currently matches the monolith. Add a deploy step, or a doctor check that diffs the two.
